SharedFlowBundle.name: ISAM-Common-ExtractClientCert
SharedFlowBundle.Description:
Reusable building block: resolves the caller's client certificate into a single canonical variable, client.cert.pem, so every SAML/JWT type embeds the same value in its request to ISAM instead of each type reading a header directly.
OUTPUT variable: client.cert.pem string, PEM-encoded X.509 certificate; null if the caller presented no certificate through either source below.
Two sources, tried in order: 1. tls.client.raw.cert -- the certificate Apigee itself received during a two-way TLS handshake on its own VirtualHost. This is the authoritative source when mutual TLS terminates AT Apigee. It is ONLY populated if the VirtualHost is configured for client auth: - Edge Private/Public Cloud: the VirtualHost's SSLInfo needs ClientAuthEnabled set to true, plus a TrustStore holding the accepted client CA chain. - Apigee X/hybrid: the environment's TLS config has propagateTLSInformation.clientProperties = true. That configuration lives on the VirtualHost/environment, not in any proxy or shared flow bundle, so it will not show up in this repo -- if client.cert.pem keeps coming back null in an environment where you expect mTLS at the gateway, check that config first, not this bundle's policies. 2. request.header.X-Client-Cert -- a PEM/URL-encoded certificate forwarded by an upstream device (a load balancer or reverse proxy in front of Apigee) that terminates mutual TLS itself. Only used as a fallback when tls.client.raw.cert is unset, i.e. Apigee did not itself terminate mTLS for this request.
Every type-specific shared flow (ISAM-SAML-Light, ISAM-SAML-User, ISAM-SAML-TP, ISAM-SAML-Technical, ISAM-JWT-SAML, ISAM-JWT-Token) calls this one via FlowCallout early in its flow, before building its request to ISAM, and reads client.cert.pem afterwards.
